title: Spontaneous Regression of Annular Basal Cell Carcinoma: A Case Report
content:
We herein present a case of annular basal cell carcinoma (BCC) with spontaneous regression on the right temporal region of a 56-year-old Japanese male. Histopathological examination revealed that the central section had no tumor cells. The sweat glands, follicles, and other cutaneous appendages were also absent. This pattern of spontaneous regression is quite uncommon, and understanding the histopathology may be important for future approaches to BCC.

IntroductionBasal cell carcinoma (BCC) is one of the most common skin neoplasms. Their ability to grow progressively and to destroy surrounding tissues can cause considerable morbidity [1]. However, there have been a few reports on partial or complete regression of BCC in the absence of any treatment [2, 3]. The precise mechanism of this phenomenon remains unclear. We hereby describe a case of annular BCC with spontaneous regression.Case ReportA 56-year-old Japanese male patient presented with an annular nodule on the right temporal region. Clinical examination revealed normal skin color in the central section of the lesion, surrounded by dark black nodules, and it had a centrifugal pattern of spread. The tumor size was 42 mm × 28 mm in diameter (Fig. 1). There was no history of previous surgery or radiation treatment to the area of the lesion. Skin biopsy from the nodules was performed, and BCC was diagnosed histopathologically. We excised the tumor with a 5-mm surgical margin to the level of adipose tissue. A skin graft from the right clavicular area was used for skin transplantation. Histopathological analysis of the tissue excised from the central section revealed no tumor nests. The cutaneous appendages, such as sebaceous glands and hair follicles, were also not found (Fig. 2a, b). The circumferential nodule consisted of hyperchromatic basaloid tumor cells distributed from the epidermis to the dermis (Fig. 2c). A mixed infiltrative and nodular type of BCC was diagnosed based on classification criteria. We performed immunohistochemical staining, and CD8+ cells (Fig. 2d) and CD68+ cells infiltrated the tumor nests.DiscussionSpontaneous regression can be defined as the complete or partial disappearance of a malignant tumor in the absence of therapy capable of inducing antineoplastic effects [1]. Curson and Weedon [4] conducted a prospective study of 400 randomly selected BCCs, and some cases showed evidence of regression. One case presented with annular BCC, similar to our case. However, observations on the histopathology of partial or complete regression in BCC have been rare. Curson and Weedon [4] described a reduction of skin appendages in the regressed areas. The findings from the normal skin-colored legion in our case were similar to this description. Histopathological analysis revealed no tumor cells infiltrating the central lesion. The sweat glands, follicles, and other cutaneous appendages were also absent. Our results from immunohistochemical staining indicated no substantial infiltration of immune cells. In contrast, CD8+ and CD68+ cells infiltrated the nodular lesions. Therefore, we suggest that CD8+ and CD68+ cells might play a role in the spontaneous regression of BCC in this case. We suggest that while the tumor diameter enlarged, CD8+ and CD68+ cells-induced tumor regression occurred simultaneously from the central section.ConclusionHere, we examined a case of annular BCC with centrifugal spread. Dark black nodules were present around the tumor circumference and expanded centrifugally. The normal-colored skin that was present in the tumor center enlarged simultaneously with the expansion of the tumor diameter. CD8+ and CD68+ cells might play a role in tumor regression, but the precise mechanism is unclear. We expect further research into the mechanism to continue.Statement of EthicsThe authors have no ethical conflicts to disclose. Informed consent was obtained from the patient. The study complied with the Declaration of Helsinki.Disclosure StatementThe authors have no conflicts of interest to declare.Author ContributionsWe all are responsible for and agree with the content and writing of the manuscript to which we all contributed significantly.

diagnosis.severity_description: annular nodule with centrifugal spread; mixed infiltrative and nodular type
diagnosis.cancer_subtype: Basal cell carcinoma (mixed infiltrative and nodular type); annular morphology
diagnosis.histology: basaloid tumor cells (hyperchromatic) distributed from epidermis to dermis; mixed infiltrative and nodular type

treatment.treatments_raw: Tumor excision with a 5-mm surgical margin to the level of adipose tissue; skin graft from the right clavicular area for transplantation.
treatment.surgery_type: Excision with 5-mm margin to adipose tissue; skin graft (right clavicular donor site)

remission_outcome.verification_detail: Clinical exam showed normal-colored skin in the central section surrounded by dark nodules; histopathology of excised central section revealed no tumor nests/cells and loss of cutaneous appendages; circumferential nodule showed basaloid tumor cells. Immunohistochemistry showed CD8+ and CD68+ cells infiltrating tumor nests in nodular lesions.
remission_outcome.tumor_response: Spontaneous regression in the central section of an annular BCC (no tumor cells in central excised tissue) with persistent tumor at circumference.
remission_outcome.tumor_size_change: Central clinically normal-colored area enlarged while overall tumor diameter expanded; excised lesion measured 42 mm × 28 mm.

validation.statistical_improbability_notes: Spontaneous regression in BCC is described as uncommon; this case documents central tumor absence within an annular lesion on histopathology.
validation.extraction_notes: This is not a whole-body remission but a partial/central spontaneous regression within an annular BCC; no follow-up/recurrence data provided.

analysis.case_summary: A 56-year-old Japanese man had an annular basal cell carcinoma on the right temple (42×28 mm) with a clinically normal-colored center and dark nodular rim. Biopsy confirmed BCC, and excision showed no tumor cells in the central area (suggesting spontaneous central regression) while the circumferential nodules contained basaloid tumor cells; CD8+ and CD68+ cells infiltrated tumor nests in nodular areas.
key_healing_factors: Histopathologically confirmed spontaneous central regression within annular BCC
Immune cell infiltration (CD8+ and CD68+) in tumor nests of nodular lesions proposed as a mechanism
unique_features: Annular BCC with centrifugal spread and simultaneous enlargement of a regressed (tumor-free) central area
Loss of cutaneous appendages (sebaceous glands, hair follicles, sweat glands) in the regressed central section
analysis.analysis_notes: The paper reports spontaneous regression occurring before/independent of treatment, but the lesion was ultimately surgically excised; timing and duration of regression are not quantified, and no long-term outcome is provided.
